title: Mathematical analysis of running performance and world running records
population: Men's 1987 world records from 60 m to the marathon, plus the progression of men's and women's records
findings: An empirical model relates performance to anaerobic capacity A, maximal aerobic power MAP and E, the reduction in peak aerobic power with the natural log of race duration T when T exceeds 420 s.
Average absolute error between actual and estimated times for men's 1987 world records from 60 m to the marathon was 0.73%.
Estimated characteristics of world-class male runners: A = 1,658 J/kg, MAP = 83.5 ml O2/kg/min, and 83.5% of MAP sustained over the marathon.
limitations: Fitted to world records of elite men, not validated on recreational runners or ultra durations; the error is in-sample.
implications: Supports a log-duration decline in sustainable power beyond about 7 min as the structural form of an endurance term, consistent with the Emig endurance index.
Candidate fallback model when only a few efforts exist (see Ruiz-Alias); do not use elite parameter values for recreational athletes.
